title: The finite smooth trace is the scalar extension of the prime-power trace
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-pur-conventions], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $e\geq1$ be the ramification index, defined by $\ell\mathcal O_E=\varpi_E^e\mathcal O_E$. Let $r\geq1$, put $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$ and $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^r\mathcal O_E=A_{E,er}$, where the last identification uses $(\ell^r)=(\varpi_E^{er})$. The map $A\to B$ is finite free [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the finite constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the compact-support functors [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the normalized finite smooth traces [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Write $T_A=A_X(d)[2d]$, $T_B=B_X(d)[2d]$ and $t_A:Rf_{!,A}T_A\to A_Y$, $t_B:Rf_{!,B}T_B\to B_Y$ for the unit-coefficient smooth traces. For every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, let
$$c_{B/A,M}:(Rf_{!,A}M)\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,B}(M\otimes_A B)$$
be the finite-free compact-support coefficient map, obtained by extension by zero followed by the proper direct-image tensor comparison, or equivalently by the compact-support projection map for $B$ [def-exchange-projection]. Under the canonical identifications $T_A\otimes_A B\cong T_B$ and $A_Y\otimes_A B\cong B_Y$, one has the equality of morphisms
$$t_B\circ c_{B/A,T_A}=t_A\otimes_A1_B.$$
Thus the normalization of the finite smooth trace over $B$ is exactly the tensor extension of the normalized prime-power trace, including its sign and Tate twist.

source.place: XVIII 2.13, equations (2.13.1)-(2.13.2), printed p. 560; Lemma 3.2.3 and Theorem 3.2.5, printed pp. 583-586: coefficient-valued trace and its purity transpose. The finite-free specialization identifies the blueprint smooth-trace normalization.
source.note: No Stacks tag states this smooth-duality normalization; this is a torsion assertion, not an adic coherence or uniqueness theorem.
